standards: OWASP Top 10 (edition per auditor knowledge, unverified)

findings.title: SQL injection in order search via unparameterised status filter
findings.evidence_snippet: const sql = "SELECT id, total, status FROM orders WHERE user_id = $1 AND status = '" + status + "'";
findings.evidence_description: The status query parameter is concatenated into the SQL text; only user_id is bound as a parameter.
findings.root_cause: Mixing string concatenation with parameter binding; no query-builder or validation layer for filters.
findings.scenario: An authenticated user calls GET /orders/search?status=x' OR '1'='1 and receives every user's orders; UNION-based payloads can read other tables reachable by the DB role.
findings.business_impact: Exposure of all customers' order data; reportable personal-data breach.
findings.technical_impact: Arbitrary read (and potentially write, depending on DB role privileges) against the orders database.
findings.mitigations: Route requires a valid JWT (src/server.js:8). No input validation, WAF config or DB role restriction found in the repository.
findings.remediation: Bind status as a parameter ($2) and validate it against an allow-list of statuses; run the API with a least-privilege DB role.

attack_path.authorization: requireAuth (any valid token); no role check
attack_path.mitigations: None effective; user_id parameter is bypassed by OR clause
attack_path.impact: Read access to all orders; further DB access depending on role

findings.verification_notes: Re-read handler and server mounting; confirmed no global validation middleware; pg does not sanitise concatenated text.

findings.title: Insecure direct object reference on GET /orders/:id
findings.evidence_snippet: const { rows } = await pool.query('SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = $1', [req.params.id]);
findings.evidence_description: Order is loaded by ID only, without filtering by req.user.sub; the result is returned in full.
findings.root_cause: Ownership enforced ad hoc per query (the pay route does it, the detail route does not); no central authorisation policy.
findings.scenario: An authenticated user iterates sequential BIGSERIAL IDs and reads other customers' orders, including psp_ref.
findings.technical_impact: Object-level authorisation bypass; the in-process cache (G-001) also serves the object to any caller.
findings.mitigations: Authentication only. IDs are sequential, which makes enumeration trivial.
findings.remediation: Filter by user_id in the query (as the pay route does at line 31) and include the user in the cache key; introduce a shared ownership-checking repository method.
findings.verification_notes: Confirmed no ownership middleware on the router; compared with the pay route, which filters by user_id.

findings.title: Payment capture called inside an open DB transaction without idempotency
findings.evidence_description: The external capture happens between BEGIN and COMMIT; if the UPDATE or COMMIT fails after a successful capture, the order remains unpaid while the customer is charged.
findings.root_cause: The transaction boundary spans a non-transactional external side effect; no idempotency key or outbox/reconciliation.
findings.scenario: PSP captures, then the DB connection drops before COMMIT; ROLLBACK leaves status pending. The client retries and is charged twice. There is also no row lock, so two concurrent pay requests can both capture.
findings.business_impact: Double charges, refunds and support load; financial reconciliation errors.
findings.technical_impact: Inconsistent state between PSP and DB; a connection is held for the full PSP latency.
findings.mitigations: None found (searched for idempotency keys, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, status checks).
findings.remediation: Mark the order 'capturing' with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE and commit; call the PSP outside the transaction with the order ID as idempotency key; record the result in a second transaction; add a reconciliation job.
findings.verification_notes: Traced the full handler; confirmed no status guard (already-paid orders can be re-captured) and no lock.

findings.title: No timeout on outbound payment provider call
findings.evidence_description: axios is called without a timeout option; the axios default is 0 (no timeout).
findings.root_cause: No shared HTTP client with default timeouts, retries or circuit breaking.
findings.scenario: The PSP slows down; each pay request holds a pooled DB connection (pool max 20, src/db.js:5) until the PSP responds, and once the pool is exhausted every endpoint stalls.
findings.business_impact: A slow payment provider can take down order browsing as well as payment.
findings.technical_impact: DB pool exhaustion and cascading latency.
findings.remediation: Create a configured axios instance (connect/read timeouts, bounded retries with idempotency key, circuit breaker) and move the call outside the transaction (J-001).
findings.runtime_verification_needed: With a stub PSP delaying 30 s, send 25 concurrent pay requests locally and observe GET /orders/:id latency; pass if reads stay < 500 ms.
findings.verification_notes: Confirmed no axios.defaults configuration anywhere in src/.

findings.title: Unbounded, never-invalidated in-process order cache
findings.evidence_description: Module-level Map with no size limit, TTL or eviction; entries are added on every cache miss and never removed or invalidated after payment updates.
findings.root_cause: Ad hoc cache without a lifecycle policy.
findings.scenario: Heap grows with the number of distinct orders read; after payment, GET returns the stale 'pending' status until restart. Multiple instances each hold diverging copies.
findings.business_impact: Customers see wrong order status; eventual memory-related restarts.
findings.technical_impact: Monotonic heap growth (leak-like retention) and stale reads.
findings.remediation: Use a bounded LRU with TTL (e.g. lru-cache) keyed by user and order, invalidated on update, or remove the cache until there is measured need.
findings.runtime_verification_needed: Run locally with --inspect, request 50k distinct order IDs, and take 3 heap snapshots; confirm the Map's retained size grows linearly and is never collected.
findings.verification_notes: Pattern confirmed statically; growth magnitude not measured (no runtime authorisation).

findings.title: Monetary amount stored as FLOAT
findings.evidence_description: orders.total uses binary floating point; the value is sent directly to the PSP.
findings.scenario: Totals such as 19.99 are stored as approximations; sums and conversions drift by fractions of a cent, so PSP amounts can mismatch.
findings.technical_impact: Rounding errors in aggregation and comparisons.
findings.remediation: Migrate to NUMERIC(12,2) or integer minor units with a currency column (expand/contract migration).
findings.verification_notes: Only one migration exists; no later ALTER.

findings.title: No index on orders.user_id used by every user-scoped query
findings.evidence_description: The schema defines only the primary key index; search filters by user_id and status.
findings.root_cause: Indexes are not reviewed alongside query patterns.
findings.scenario: As the table grows, every search becomes a sequential scan.
findings.business_impact: Search latency grows with total order volume, not per-user volume.
findings.technical_impact: Sequential scans; increased DB CPU and I/O.
findings.remediation: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY orders_user_status_idx ON orders (user_id, status).
findings.runtime_verification_needed: EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the search query on a local copy with ≥ 1M rows.
findings.verification_notes: Searched all SQL files for CREATE INDEX; none.

findings.title: No automated tests despite a configured test script
findings.evidence_description: A test script exists but the repository contains no test files, so authorisation, injection and payment paths are untested.
findings.root_cause: Testing not part of the definition of done.
findings.scenario: Regressions such as F-001 and F-002 ship without detection.
findings.business_impact: Higher defect escape rate on revenue-critical flows.
findings.technical_impact: No safety net for the remediation work in this report.
findings.remediation: Add integration tests (testcontainers Postgres) for search, detail ownership and pay idempotency before remediating.
findings.verification_notes: Searched for *.test.js, *.spec.js, test/ and __tests__; none found.

findings.title: JWT verification pins algorithm, audience and issuer
findings.evidence_description: jwt.verify is called with an explicit RS256 allow-list plus aud and iss checks, preventing alg-confusion and token reuse across services.
findings.business_impact: Reduces token forgery and confusion risk.
findings.remediation: Preserve. Consider adding clock-tolerance and key rotation (JWKS).
findings.verification_notes: Confirmed library version 9.x enforces exp by default.

findings.title: Committed environment file contains secrets
findings.evidence_description: The file is .env.example with empty or placeholder values only; there is no secret material and git history has a single commit.
findings.verification_notes: Rejected by verifier: example file, no values; git log -p shows no real .env.
